**Predict first.** With γ = 0.9 and tol = 10⁻⁶, the evaluation below stops after a little over 100 iterations. If you move γ to 0.99, will it need about twice as many iterations, ten times as many, or a hundred times as many? And if you keep γ = 0.9 but make tol 100 times smaller? Write down both guesses, then use the sliders.

The model has two states, 0 and 1, and a fixed policy π. From state 0 you stay or move to state 1 with probability 0.5 each, and the mean reward is 1. From state 1 you move to state 0 with probability 0.1 and stay with probability 0.9, and the mean reward is 0. Evaluation starts from V~0~ = 0 and applies T^π^ ([@eq-tpi]) until ‖V~k+1~ − V~k~‖~∞~ < tol ([@eq-stop]). The error is measured against the exact V^π^ from the 2 × 2 linear solve ([@eq-exact]).

$$
P_\pi = \begin{pmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.1 & 0.9 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad
r_\pi = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}
$$

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Inputs.range ties its visible <label> to the number box; the slider gets the same name.
function labeledRange(extent, options) {
  const form = Inputs.range(extent, options);
  form.querySelector("input[type=range]").setAttribute("aria-label", options.label);
  return form;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof gamma = labeledRange([0.5, 0.99], {value: 0.9, step: 0.01, label: "Discount γ"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof logTol = labeledRange([-8, -2], {value: -6, step: 1, label: "log₁₀ of tol"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The two-state model and the run: exact V^pi, then iterative evaluation from V_0 = 0.
contraction = {
  const P = [[0.5, 0.5], [0.1, 0.9]];
  const r = [1, 0];
  const g = Math.round(gamma * 100) / 100; // the slider's value, without float dust
  const tol = 10 ** logTol;
  // V^pi = (I - g P)^-1 r, solved exactly for 2 x 2 (Cramer's rule)
  const a = 1 - g * P[0][0], b = -g * P[0][1];
  const c = -g * P[1][0], d = 1 - g * P[1][1];
  const det = a * d - b * c;
  const vpi = [(d * r[0] - b * r[1]) / det, (a * r[1] - c * r[0]) / det];
  const start = Math.max(Math.abs(vpi[0]), Math.abs(vpi[1])); // ||V_0 - V^pi||, V_0 = 0
  const rows = [{k: 0, error: start, bound: start}];
  let v = [0, 0];
  for (let k = 1; k <= 100000; k++) {
    const next = [
      r[0] + g * (P[0][0] * v[0] + P[0][1] * v[1]),
      r[1] + g * (P[1][0] * v[0] + P[1][1] * v[1])
    ];
    const step = Math.max(Math.abs(next[0] - v[0]), Math.abs(next[1] - v[1]));
    v = next;
    const error = Math.max(Math.abs(v[0] - vpi[0]), Math.abs(v[1] - vpi[1]));
    rows.push({k, error, bound: g ** k * start});
    if (step < tol) {
      return {g, tol, vpi, start, rows, k, error, guarantee: (g * tol) / (1 - g)};
    }
  }
}
```

[[]{style="display:inline-block; width:2.25rem; vertical-align:middle; border-top:3px solid var(--prl-series-1);"} Error ‖V~k~ − V^π^‖~∞~]{.demo-key style="display:inline-block; margin-right:1.25rem;"}
[[]{style="display:inline-block; width:2.25rem; vertical-align:middle; border-top:3px dashed var(--prl-series-2);"} Bound γ^k^ ‖V~0~ − V^π^‖~∞~ ([@eq-iteration-bound])]{.demo-key style="display:inline-block; margin-right:1.25rem;"}
[[]{style="display:inline-block; width:2.25rem; vertical-align:middle; border-top:3px dotted var(--prl-neutral);"} Guarantee at the stop, γ·tol/(1 − γ)]{.demo-key style="display:inline-block;"}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {rows, k, guarantee} = contraction;
  const sup = (n) => String(n).replace(/[-0-9]/g, (ch) => "⁻⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹"["-0123456789".indexOf(ch)]);
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width,
    height: 320,
    marginTop: 34,
    marginLeft: 56,
    marginRight: 16,
    marginBottom: 44,
    style: "font-family: inherit; font-size: 14px; color: var(--prl-text); background: transparent; --plot-background: var(--prl-bg);",
    x: {label: "Iteration k", labelAnchor: "center", labelArrow: "none", domain: [0, k], nice: true},
    y: {
      type: "log",
      domain: [1e-10, 1e2],
      ticks: [1e-10, 1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1, 1e2],
      tickFormat: (t) => (t === 1 ? "1" : "10" + sup(Math.round(Math.log10(t)))),
      label: "Error (log scale)",
      labelArrow: "none",
      grid: true
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([guarantee], {stroke: "var(--prl-neutral)", strokeWidth: 2.5, strokeDasharray: "2,5", strokeLinecap: "round"}),
      Plot.line(rows, {x: "k", y: "bound", stroke: "var(--prl-series-2)", strokeWidth: 2.5, strokeDasharray: "9,6"}),
      Plot.line(rows, {x: "k", y: "error", stroke: "var(--prl-series-1)", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot([rows[k]], {x: "k", y: "error", r: 6, fill: "var(--prl-series-1)", stroke: "var(--prl-bg)", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text([rows[k]], {x: "k", y: "error", text: (d) => `stop: k = ${d.k}`, textAnchor: "end", dx: -10, dy: 16, fill: "currentColor", fontWeight: 600})
    ]
  });
  // One name for the whole chart (the readout below carries the numbers). Plot also
  // names its <g> groups, which ARIA does not allow on a role-less <g>.
  for (const node of chart.querySelectorAll("[aria-label]")) node.removeAttribute("aria-label");
  chart.setAttribute("role", "img");
  chart.setAttribute(
    "aria-label",
    `Error against iteration on a log scale, from 0 to ${k} iterations. The error and the bound both fall in straight lines; the run stops at iteration ${k}, below the guarantee line.`
  );
  return chart;
}
```

::: {#demo-contraction-readout .demo-readout aria-live="polite" style="font-weight:600; margin:0.5rem 0 1rem;"}
The demo needs JavaScript. With it off: at γ = 0.9 and tol = 10⁻⁶, evaluation stops after 116 iterations.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Writes the sentence into the persistent aria-live region above, so a screen reader
// announces each new result (a region re-created on every change is not announced).
contractionReadout = {
  const {g, tol, vpi, k, error, guarantee} = contraction;
  const e = (x) => x.toExponential(1);
  const text =
    `γ = ${g.toFixed(2)}, tol = ${e(tol)}. Stops after ${k} iterations; ` +
    `final error ≤ γ·tol/(1 − γ) = ${e(guarantee)}, and the actual final error is ${e(error)}. ` +
    `Exact values: ${vpi[0].toFixed(3)} in state 0, ${vpi[1].toFixed(3)} in state 1.`;
  const el = document.getElementById("demo-contraction-readout");
  if (el) el.textContent = text;
  return text;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="What to notice (open after you predict)"}
- On the log axis both lines are straight: each iteration multiplies the error by about γ, as [@eq-iteration-bound] says. The error runs parallel to the bound, a little below it.
- Going from γ = 0.9 to 0.99 takes about ten times as many iterations (116 to 1,198 at tol = 10⁻⁶): the count grows like 1/(1 − γ).
- A tolerance 100 times smaller costs only a fixed number of extra iterations, about log(100)/log(1/γ): 44 at γ = 0.9 (43 in the run), 458 at γ = 0.99.
- The run stops just under the dotted line γ·tol/(1 − γ) ([@eq-stop]). At γ = 0.99 that line is 99 × tol, so a small tol alone does not promise a small error.
:::
